119.0.s.en: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

119.0.0.en: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD. Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart.

119.0.1.en: 1- As Christ began His Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes, David begins this psalm by pronouncing blessed the perfect, that is, how happy are those who walk in the way of perfection, for God grants them to be without outward blemish, even if they have their inward weaknesses. Walking in the way of perfection is walking in the law of God, and even keeping it, not only in the mind but applying it in life.

119.0.2.en: 2- Whoever keeps God's commandments in his mind and repeats them with his tongue, they enter into his feelings, so he seeks them in prayer with his whole heart. The one who is purified by meditating on the commandment is able to behold God, because seeking with the whole heart means that the heart is attached to God, and therefore he receives the grace of beholding God, because the heart does not halt between two opinions, that is, God and the world, but has chosen God alone to live by Him in the midst of the world, and is neither affected by its lusts nor subject to them.

119.1.0.en: They also do no iniquity: they walk in his ways.

119.1.1.en: 1- Whoever loves the word of God and walks in the way of perfection lives in the light and does not love darkness, so he keeps far from sins and does not fall into them, at least in deeds or in words, even if he is exposed to falling into them in thought or in the heart.

119.1.2.en: 2- The one who walks in righteousness is concerned to be in the way of God, that is, holding fast to His commandments, and does not want to walk in his ways, that is, the ways of the world, which are the various lusts. For the way of God is one, and it is Christ, whereas the evil ways of the world are many.

119.2.0.en: Thou hast commanded us to keep thy precepts diligently.

119.2.1.en: God asks His children to keep His commandments fully, that is, with all exactness, so that they do not leave out any part of them or neglect any one of His commandments, and strive to carry them out with all their hearts; and He helps them to enjoy delightful depths in them, so that they are in constant joy.

119.3.0.en: O that my ways were directed to keep thy statutes!

119.3.1.en: Since David believed in the importance of keeping the commandments to the full, he asked God's help to remain firm in keeping the commandments, so that he would not fall short in carrying them out, for if he fell short he would be exposed to the warfare of Satan and fall into various sins. Here the importance of the work of grace together with spiritual striving appears, for the striver cannot do without the work of grace, and grace works in those who love God's commandments and strive to carry them out.

119.4.0.en: Then shall I not be ashamed, when I have respect unto all thy commandments.

119.4.1.en: If the work of grace is united with spiritual striving, a person is encouraged to enter into God's commandments, that is, His word, so he deepens in the knowledge of God and discovers the beauty of His commandments, that is, he sees Christ the Word of God and enjoys fellowship with Him. And this gives him the hope that on the day of judgment he will not be ashamed when he looks upon Christ the Judge, and will find a place for himself in His Kingdom. For shame accompanies sin, as happened at the fall of Adam and Eve, whereas keeping the commandment keeps a person away from shame and gives him the joy of being with God.

119.5.0.en: I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, when I shall have learned thy righteous judgments.

119.5.1.en: 1- When I learn Your judgments, that is, Your commandments and Your word, I understand and know the purpose hidden in them. And this makes me upright in my feelings and in my thoughts, and it shows in my conduct and my speech, and I am no longer disturbed by the errors that are spread in the world and its strange ideas, because I am holding fast to, and fortified by, the righteous word of God.

119.5.2.en: 2- Then, as I discover justice and truth through Your judgments, I thank You and praise You for Your grace toward me, and I even feel my weakness and my unworthiness of all these favors, so my praise of You increases. And I also praise God who enlightened my inner eye and showed me His person and the greatness of eternal life, so I am not disturbed by the sins of the world and its changes, and I thank Him with all my heart, with uprightness and without being defiled by any evil thought.

119.6.0.en: I will keep thy statutes: O forsake me not utterly.

119.6.1.en: 1- At the end of this section David declares the intention of his heart and his complete readiness to keep God's commandments in his thought and heart and also in his conduct.

119.6.2.en: 2- He entreats God that, however much he strives to hold fast to the commandment, he is weak and liable to fall short and err, to the point that God may forsake him in order to discipline and warn him, so that he returns to Him in repentance. But he asks God not to leave him completely and reject him, but if He forsakes him partially, to return and have mercy on him and help him to keep the commandments, because he longs to live by them.

119.6.3.en: Memorize a verse every day, one that touches your heart when you read the Holy Bible. It is a message from God to you, that you may live by it. Repeat it throughout the day and try to apply it, and God will support you and even reveal to you new experiences of His love and care for you.

119.6.4.en: The second section (Beth): How a young man lives (vv. 9-16). The aim:

119.6.5.en: After showing the blessings of keeping the commandment, it focuses on the young man, full of vitality, that he may care for the commandment, so he acquires it and suffers in it, and so praises God, then proclaims it to those around him, and so rejoices in it and repeats it at all times and lives in the enjoyment of fellowship with God.

119.7.0.en: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

119.7.1.en: Cleanse: set straight, or make his way right and sound.

119.7.3.en: 1- The young man is full of vitality, but he is exposed to falling into lusts and rushing into unsound actions, so how can he purify his way, that is, walk in a right, upright way that pleases God? He cannot do this except by relying on the word of God and applying it in his life.

119.7.4.en: 2- The young man also signifies the Gentiles who have newly entered the faith, for in order to cleanse their way they need to hold strongly to the word of God.

119.8.0.en: With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.

119.8.1.en: 1- The young man is full of vitality, so he seeks God with his whole heart, that is, with all his being, his feelings and his thoughts, and not merely an outward impulse. He carries out what Christ said, and what is stated in the Book of Deuteronomy, "Thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart"... (Deut 6:5).

119.8.2.en: 2- If a person seeks God with all his heart, God will not forsake him, but on the contrary hastens to him and supports him; he is not exposed to wandering or to departing from God's commandments, but on the contrary God establishes him in His commandments and makes him grow in the knowledge of them.

119.9.0.en: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.

119.9.1.en: 1- Why did the young man hide God's word in his heart?

119.9.2.en: a - He feels that the word of God is very precious, so he keeps it in his depths.

119.9.3.en: b - So that his thought and feelings may be saturated with the word of God, and therefore pure.

119.9.4.en: c - So that he may always meditate on the word of God and murmur it (lahaj), that is, repeat it so that his understanding grows.

119.9.5.en: d - Since he is filled inwardly with the word of God, this word comes out spontaneously in his speech and his deeds.

119.9.6.en: e - The spirit of hiddenness is very important, because the spiritual young man does not seek the glory of men, but lives always in humility.

119.9.7.en: 2- It is not enough for the young man to know the word of God inwardly; it must appear in his speech and in his works, so that he is a light to the world and the salt of the earth; for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh (Mt 12:34).

119.10.0.en: Blessed art thou, O LORD: teach me thy statutes.

119.10.1.en: 1- Since the young man is satisfied with the word of God and has lived by it within and without, he rejoices greatly and thanks God and blesses Him. His blessing of God expresses the young man's joy and satisfaction with the word of God.

119.10.2.en: 2- The young man takes courage and asks God to teach him how to draw near to Him and how to walk before Him in holy worship, so He teaches him the rites and the spirituality of worship, that his understanding and growth in the knowledge of God may increase.

119.11.0.en: With my lips have I declared all the judgments of thy mouth.

119.11.2.en: Since the young man is filled with the word of God, it becomes natural for spiritual teachings arising from God's commandments to appear in his speech. Even if the young man's words and dealings seem ordinary, they contain the thought of God, His judgments and His teachings, so they light the way for those around him and make God known to all. This is what the Samaritan woman did when she believed and enjoyed seeing Christ: she went and told her people the holy good news (Jn 4:29).

119.12.0.en: I have rejoiced in the way of thy testimonies, as much as in all riches.

119.12.1.en: As much as in all riches: more than, and above, all the riches in the world.

119.12.2.en: 1- When the word of God and His testimonies satisfy the heart, and a person lives by them, they give him a true and complete joy, so he sets out in unceasing hope to live with God.

119.12.3.en: 2- This joy is above all the joys of the world and above all material wealth, because it is a deep inward joy that makes a person happy and remains in him, unlike the temporary, passing joys of the world. Therefore David preferred the word of God and being with Him to all his wealth, and devoted all his possessions to preparing the materials for building the house of God, which his son Solomon would build; for the testimonies of God are better than all the wealth and material things of the world.

119.13.0.en: I will meditate in thy precepts, and have respect unto thy ways. I will delight myself in thy statutes: I will not forget thy word.

119.13.2.en: 1- In the end the young man loves the word of God, so he meditates on it at all times, and observes the ways of God's holy children in order to learn from them how to live by the word of God. And when he offers worship to God he feels the joy of being in His hands, and He gives him peace and joy, and worship becomes delightful, so he holds fast all the more to the word of God in his thought, his speech and all his life.

119.13.3.en: 2- Thus we see the advice given to the young man by the prophet David about the word of God, which is:

119.13.4.en: a - Acquiring the word of God (v. 9).

119.13.5.en: b - Longing for the word of God and seeking it with the whole heart (v. 10).

119.13.6.en: c - Hiding the word of God in order to meditate on it, so that it protects him from sin (v. 11).

119.13.7.en: d - The word of God teaches the young man praise and thanksgiving (v. 12).

119.13.8.en: e - Witnessing and speaking the word of God (v. 13).

119.13.9.en: f - Rejoicing in the word of God (v. 14).

119.13.10.en: g - Repeating the word of God at all times (v. 15).

119.13.11.en: h - Enjoying and delighting in the worship of God (v. 16).

119.13.12.en: May you repeat the verse you chose every day, occupying your thought with it, so that your heart and feelings are touched, until it is turned into practical life in your conduct, and you even delight and rejoice in it, so that it lives in you and you live by it.

119.13.13.en: The third section (Gimel): Comfort in the worker's exile (vv. 17-24). The aim:

119.13.14.en: After charging the young man to keep God's commandment, it reminds him that he is a stranger on the earth. This increases his attachment to the word of God, so he needs to remember God's kindnesses and asks Him to reveal to him the depths of His word, so his longing for Him increases. And he asks God to remove reproach and shame from him and to keep him from his enemies, so he rejoices and communes with God, who guides him in his life.

119.14.0.en: Deal bountifully with thy servant, that I may live, and keep thy word.

119.14.1.en: 1- God dealt bountifully with David and rewarded him by anointing him king though he was a shepherd of sheep, and gave him strength to kill the lion and the bear, then Goliath, and rescued him from the hand of Saul and Absalom. All these divine kindnesses made him live, sit on the throne, govern the kingdom and triumph over his enemies.

119.14.2.en: 2- David also asks for a spiritual divine kindness, which is the spiritual life, that God may help him to keep His commandments and His orders, so that he may enjoy fellowship with Him.

119.14.3.en: 3- David thanked God for His kindness, and was kind to Saul, who fell twice into his hand, and he did not harm him. And he asks God to reward him with His many mercies.

119.14.4.en: 4- God's kindnesses give strength and life to David and to everyone who believes in God, and this helps him to hold fast to God's orders and keep them alive in his life, as a response to the divine love.

119.15.0.en: Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.

119.15.1.en: 1- David asks God to open his eyes, that is, to grant him spiritual enlightenment, and this shows the humility of David, who confesses that in his weakness he suffers from the darkness of sin and needs God to open his eye.

119.15.2.en: 2- The opening of the eyes means that a person receives the simple vision, that is, he sees everything through the lens of God, or as God sees it. So he sees good things and thanks God for them, and he also sees sins, and prays that God may take them away.

119.15.3.en: 3- When a person receives spiritual enlightenment he is able to understand the law of God, and he discovers new depths in it every time he reads it. And above all this the reader sees, in the Old Testament and also the New Testament, Christ hidden behind the words, of whom the prophets prophesied and whom the Apostles preached. Therefore the Church ordained that the priest pray the Litany of the Gospel, before we hear the Gospel, in which the priest asks God to give His people understanding of the words of the Gospel; and the priest likewise prays secret prayers during the reading of the other readings, which are the Pauline Epistle, the Catholic Epistle and the Acts, for the same purpose, which is the understanding of the word of God.

119.16.0.en: I am a stranger in the earth: hide not thy commandments from me.

119.16.1.en: 1- David feels that he is a stranger on the earth though he is a king, because of his belief that his true homeland is heaven. This was also the feeling of the great fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, therefore they lived in tents. And God ordained for His people in the Old Testament a great feast, called the Feast of Tabernacles, that they might remember their exile in the world. In the New Testament also St. Paul says that we are "strangers and pilgrims"... (Heb 11:13), and he even says, "if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved" (2 Cor 5:1).

119.16.2.en: 2- A stranger needs signs along the road so that he does not get lost. And the signs of the spiritual road to the Kingdom are God's commandments, so David asks that God not hide them from him, but show them clearly, because of his weakness as a stranger.

119.16.3.en: 3- A stranger wants to know the greatest amount of information about the homeland he wants to reach; and in our case here, the homeland is heaven, because we were born of God in Baptism, and the greatest information is found in God's commandments, which lift us up to heaven, so we get rid of the lusts of the earth, and by lightening our load we are able to hasten to heaven, like a light bird that rises on its wings to the heights after leaving the burdens of the earth.

119.17.0.en: My soul breaketh for the longing that it hath unto thy judgments at all times.

119.17.1.en: Breaketh: that is, it has been crushed and ground, so it lost its outward form because it became greatly compressed.

119.17.2.en: 1- David longs to know God's judgments and commandments, which express God, and he is so eager for God that he was crushed, so there was no strength left in him, and he was utterly humbled, asking God to make known to him His judgments. This shows his intense longing for the word of God, and that he longs with all his heart.

119.17.3.en: 2- David longs for God's judgments because he loves them very much, and his heart is attached to them, and he needs them at all times, for he cannot imagine his life without them, because God is his life, and His judgments are what bring him to heaven, that is, life with God for ever. And by this longing his spirit is enlightened and he turns away from everything.

119.18.0.en: Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments.

119.18.1.en: 1- What hinders a person from God's commandments is:

119.18.2.en: a - Pride, so he rejects God and His word, and justifies his sins.

119.18.3.en: b - Ignorance and error, and lack of longing to know the word of God.

119.18.4.en: This makes a person deserving of God's curse, that is, God forsakes him and he is deprived of being with Him.

119.18.5.en: 2- It mentions pride as the chief cause of God's curse, because it is the first of the sins that brought down Satan, and likewise the first man, Adam and Eve. For this reason Christ stressed to us that we should learn humility from Him (Mt 11:29).

119.19.0.en: Roll away from me reproach and contempt; for I have kept thy testimonies.

119.19.1.en: 1- The one who keeps the testimonies of the Lord and lives in righteousness is mocked by the wicked, the people of the world, and in their eyes he comes to be in disgrace and shame. So this righteous man asks God to remove this disgrace and shame from him, so that the wicked may understand their sin and turn back from their error and believe in God, and, on the other hand, so that the righteous may be established in the life of righteousness.

119.19.2.en: And David's use of the word "roll away" reminds us of the work of God and His grace, for by His power He first rolled the stone away from the tomb of Christ to abolish the disgrace and shame of death, and it is He who with His outstretched arm rolled away the shame of the people of the children of Israel in Egypt and brought them out of humiliation. And so He lifted the shame from every repentant sinner and clothed him with the first robe. Be strong and take courage, beloved, that Christ may roll away from you the disgrace of sin.

119.20.0.en: Princes also did sit and speak against me: but thy servant did meditate in thy statutes. Thy testimonies also are my delight and my counsellors.

119.20.1.en: 1- The princes who took counsel against David and said evil and harmful things about him were Saul and his helpers. In this he is a type of Christ, against whom the chief priests, the priests, the scribes and the Pharisees sat and took counsel to entangle Him in a word, and then also to kill Him. And all the men of God were exposed to this, such as the princes of the kingdom of Persia, who took counsel against Daniel and cast him into the den, and the princes of Judah, who took counsel against Jeremiah and cast him into prison and into the pit.

119.20.2.en: 2- David, Christ and all the righteous of the Old and New Testaments took a positive course, which is:

119.20.3.en: a- Communing with God's statutes, that is, worshiping Him, through prayer and reading the word of God.

119.20.4.en: b- Meditating on and delighting in God's testimonies, that is, His commandments and His word.

119.20.5.en: c- Relying on the word of God as the source of counsel and guidance in life.

119.20.6.en: Be careful to remain positive in your life, however much the wicked surround you or threaten you; do not fear, but hold fast to your prayers and to reading the word of God, and it will guide you and even bring you into delight in fellowship with God, even in the midst of afflictions.

119.20.7.en: The fourth section (Daleth): The risen life (vv. 25-32). The aim:

119.20.8.en: After supporting the young man in his exile in the midst of the world, it declares to him here the word of God, which is able to raise him up from his toils and sorrows and give him life. So he desires to know God's commandments and worship, and suffers in his works, and keeps away from evil, and walks in the way of truth, and so his heart is enlarged with love for all.

119.21.0.en: My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.

119.21.1.en: 1- David expresses the degree of psychological pain that he reached, as his soul, and not only his body, cleaves to the dust; that is, he is in intense distress, whether from the harshness of his enemies' threats and their troubling of him, or from the distress resulting from his falling into sin and regretting it.

119.21.2.en: 2- If the serpent crawls on the earth, sin makes a person cleave to the dust while he does not feel it, being occupied with its pleasure. But the repentant expresses his repentance by prostrations (metanoias) when his body cleaves to the dust of the earth, and his soul also cleaves to the dust in regret over his sin, and so he receives God's mercies; for he resembles the dead whose body cleaves to the dust of the earth, but he rises from the earth by repentance and stands giving thanks to Christ, risen from the dead, who raised him up. Therefore this verse is prayed at the funeral of priests.

119.21.3.en: 3- Despite the clinging of David's soul to the dust, he did not lose his hope in the power of God that gives him life, according to His promise and also by His life-giving word. In this he became a type of Christ, whose body cleaved to the dust in the tomb and then rose alive on the third day. And just as God gave life to the people of Nineveh when they repented, and likewise to the Prodigal Son, and to Daniel whom He brought out of the den, and to the Three Youths from the furnace of fire.

119.21.4.en: 4- Everyone who prays for others feels this verse, as his soul cleaves to the dust in humility before God, that He may bring back those who are far away, rescue them from their problems and give them a new, joyful life.

119.22.0.en: (I have declared my ways, and thou heardest me: teach me thy statutes. Make me to understand the way of thy precepts: so shall I talk of thy wondrous works.

119.22.1.en: 1- Declaring my ways means confessing my sins, and also presenting all my problems and needs to God, and He answers me as a Father, forgiving my sins and solving my problems.

119.22.2.en: 2- My ways can be my spiritual principles and everything God has taught me. When I declare, that is, live by them, He answers all my requests and needs.

119.22.3.en: 3- Since I have become accustomed to opening all my life to God, and have experienced His answer to my requests, I therefore ask Him to teach me His statutes, that is, His worship, for I never want to be far from Him; and I also ask Him to make me understand His commandments so that I may live by them, and then I experience their sweetness, so I commune with Him through them and thank Him for His wonderful works with me.

119.23.0.en: (My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.

119.23.1.en: 1- David likens himself to a candle that melts drop by drop, that is, he is in intense sorrow over his sins, or over all that he suffers. And this sorrow, despite its intensity, has hope in God, so it is a holy sorrow.

119.23.2.en: 2- David's hope in God appears when he asks Him to raise him up from his sorrows according to His commandments, that is, to rise to live by the word of God. For the source of his rising is the word of God by which he will live, and he thanks God for His grace.

119.24.0.en: (Remove from me the way of lying, and have mercy on me by thy law.

119.24.1.en: 1- David loved God, therefore he rejected the sin of lying, even in thought, and asked God to remove from him thoughts of lying so that he would not do it. And by lying he also means every other sin. For he wants to live in purity so that he may have a place in heaven with God.

119.24.2.en: 2- David declares to God: if I have fallen into the sin of lying or any other sin, then forgive me and have mercy on me by Your testimonies. And grant me to read and meditate on Your word, so that I live in purity.

119.25.0.en: (I have chosen the way of truth: thy judgments have I laid before me.

119.25.1.en: 1- Here David's positive attitude appears in choosing the way of truth, and not only choosing the way of truth, which is the way of God, but also setting before him God's judgments, that is, His word, as a goal by which to live and from which not to depart. In this he was established in the straight way and kept far from the evil to which he referred in the previous verse.

119.26.0.en: (I have stuck unto thy testimonies: O LORD, put me not to shame.

119.26.1.en: 1- David was not content with choosing the way of truth and setting God's judgments before him, but he also clung to His testimonies, so the word of God became very close to him, and he loved it with all his heart.

119.26.2.en: 2- Despite all this love for the word of God, David as a human being is still liable to fall into sin, and therefore he asks for God's forgiveness and support, so that he may not be put to shame by falling into sin, and may receive forgiveness.

119.27.0.en: (I run in the way of thy commandments, for thou hast enlarged my heart.

119.27.2.en: 1- At the conclusion of this section David felt the importance of the word of God and his attachment to it, so that he began to run in its way in order to be satisfied by it; even if the way of keeping and carrying out the commandments needs striving, and he meets obstacles in carrying them out, he holds to the narrow gate and the difficult way because of his love for God.

119.27.3.en: 2- What encouraged David to run in God's way, however difficult the striving, was that God gave him faith and peace in his heart, and even enlarged his heart to love God and all people, so he enjoyed joy; indeed, in proportion to the difficulty of the striving, the grace of God granted him a heart wide with love for all and constant joy.

119.27.4.en: Life is hidden for you in the word of God, so in proportion to your occupation with reading it and meditating on it you taste peace, and live with spiritual feelings and zeal, and enjoy being with God.

119.27.5.en: The fifth section (He): The guide of life (vv. 33-40). The aim:

119.27.6.en: When the spiritual person has experienced the work of the word of God in him, which raises him up from his sorrows and toils, he loves the word of God, so it becomes a guide for him on the way of life, and he asks to learn, understand and be trained in keeping the word of God, so he keeps away from the vanities of the world and lives in the fear of God and true repentance, and his heart is kindled with desire for God's judgments.

119.28.0.en: (Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it unto the end.

119.28.1.en: 1- David shows his need to learn and to be a disciple, for this leads to his humility and his inclination to know God and to live with Him. And he wants to learn the way of God's statutes, for learning continues throughout life: that he may know how to worship God and walk by His law.

119.28.2.en: 2- Perhaps David longed, in the spirit of prophecy, to learn also the way of Christian worship, which is in spirit and truth.

119.28.3.en: 3- This learning needs spiritual striving, because it will continue throughout life, and on its basis the worship in heaven will be, that is, he acquires the spirit of the love of God, and how to be in His presence with prayers, praises and meditation on God.

119.29.0.en: (Give me understanding, and I shall keep thy law; yea, I shall observe it with my whole heart.

119.29.1.en: 1- David asks not only to learn the worship of God, but also to understand His law, so that he may worship Him with his tongue and mind. This is by observing His law as applied in the lives of His righteous children, in addition to observing the law, that is, meditating on its meanings, that God may grant him to understand it.

119.29.2.en: 2- After David understands God's law he needs to keep it, not only in his mind but practically in his life, feeling it in his heart and applying it in his conduct, so that it becomes a living part of his life, indeed it is his life.

119.30.0.en: (Make me to go in the path of thy commandments; for therein do I delight.

119.30.1.en: 1- David loved God's commandments, so he knew them and understood them by God's guidance of him, but he wants to live by them, and this is not an easy matter, but needs training through the days. And God is the trainer, as He is the One who knows His children and makes them understand His commandments, and also cares for them and supports them with spiritual exercises to apply the commandment, and also helps them in the spiritual striving because of their love and delight in His commandments.

119.30.2.en: 2- Whoever understands God's commandments turns to them to keep them, and even turns to training in them, and God reveals to him new depths in them during this training. From all this we understand that David, in his freedom, asks to know, understand and be trained; therefore the grace of God works in him and gives him all that he needs. For grace works with the one who wills and asks. And God helps the one who asks and strives, not only in training in the commandment, but He increases his desire to learn (Phil 2:13).

119.31.0.en: (Incline my heart unto thy testimonies, and not to covetousness. Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.

119.31.1.en: 1- David takes courage, having tasted the sweetness of God's word, and asks Him to incline his feelings to His testimonies, so that they become the sole goal of his life, and therefore his soul is not occupied with material gain as a goal, and does not turn aside to wronging people in order to obtain this gain.

119.31.2.en: 2- Since David set God's commandments as his goal, his eyes turned from the vanities of the world, and he felt that all the gains of the earth are vain, so God's way became open to him to live always by His commandments. This is what happened with all the saints in both Testaments, whereas the opposite, that is, being occupied with the vanities of the world, is the conduct of the wicked, as in the days of Noah, and when Samson loved the lust of women, and likewise when David fell into adultery, or Judas Iscariot in the love of money.

119.32.0.en: (Stablish thy word unto thy servant, who is devoted to thy fear.

119.32.1.en: 1- When David tasted the grace of God, which turned his eyes from evil, and lived the feelings of repentance, he dared, with the boldness of the son who fears his father and reveres him, to ask Him to establish and fulfill His promises to him, and to all His children, which He spoke in His commandments, so that He gives him life with Him on earth and for ever.

119.33.0.en: (Turn away my reproach which I fear: for thy judgments are good.

119.33.1.en: 1- David entreats God to remove from him the disgrace of sin that clung to him, of which God had earlier warned him by His commandments, and to remove from him and from all the righteous also the reproaches of the wicked, which have no value; indeed whoever bears them receives a reward from God, for the true disgrace is the disgrace of sin.

119.33.2.en: 2- The removal of the disgrace of sin is by God's good judgments, which guide him so that he takes heed, keeps away from sin and offers repentance, so God forgives him, and then he walks by God's good commandments which satisfy his soul, so he lives and rejoices in them.

119.34.0.en: (Behold, I have longed after thy precepts: quicken me in thy righteousness.

119.34.1.en: 1- Since David held fast to God's commandments, God granted him a desire for the commandment, so he walked in its way and delighted in it, and discovered his sins, so he rejected them and hated them, and received forgiveness of them through the Cross, which he saw in the spirit of prophecy, and on which Christ satisfied divine justice and gave life to everyone who believes in Him.

119.34.2.en: Examine yourself by the word of God that you read in the Holy Bible, and it will lead you to repentance and remove your sins in the sacrament of confession and Holy Communion, so that you live with God in a life of daily repentance.

119.34.3.en: The sixth section (Vav): Witnessing to the word of God (vv. 41-48). The aim:

119.34.4.en: After a person has submitted to the guidance of the word of God he becomes able here to bear witness by the word of God even before kings, so that the word of God has become for him delight, love and communion, and also practical life.

119.35.0.en: (Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, even thy salvation, according to thy word. So shall I have wherewith to answer him that reproacheth me: for I trust in thy word.

119.35.1.en: 1- David asks for God's mercy, by which he receives his salvation, as God promised him through all the prophecies of the Old Testament. David's request for mercy shows his repentance, his humility, and his faith in God's mercy and in His salvation that would be accomplished on the Cross in the fullness of time.

119.35.2.en: 2- When David, and every believer, receives God's mercy and salvation, he is able by the power of the Spirit of God to answer the demons and all the wicked who reproach him and try to make him fall into despair, and by this he bears witness to God who supports him because he trusted in His commandments. And the more he bears witness to God the Savior, the more he holds fast to His commandments, and His mercies overflow upon him, and he is gradually saved from every evil and lives for God.

119.35.3.en: 3- Christ was exposed to many reproaches from the Jews, but He completed His way to the Cross, to grant the mercy and salvation to mankind who believe in Him.

119.36.0.en: (And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; for I have hoped in thy judgments. So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever.

119.36.1.en: 1- David shows his holding fast to the word of God, which is the word of truth, as he asks God to establish it in his heart and on his tongue. And even in the midst of afflictions in which a person can fall into murmuring, or doubt, or failure to understand some of God's judgments, God's word is not utterly taken from him. Rather, if he speaks a vain word, he returns and bears witness to God, and his heart remains believing in the word of God and awaiting His salvation, which will be completed at the proper time, and which solves his problems on earth and then completes their solution when he reaches the Kingdom. Thus the prophets, God's children, held fast to the word of truth whatever they endured, even if they sacrificed their lives, like the prophet Isaiah, whom King Manasseh sawed asunder, and the prophet Jeremiah, whom they stoned in Egypt, and John the Baptist, whose head Herod cut off.

119.36.2.en: 2- David wishes to keep God's law continually for ever, that is, throughout life in all the circumstances of life, whether in strength or weakness, in health or sickness... and he continues to enjoy meditating on the word of God for ever, that is, he enjoys seeing Christ the Word of God in heaven.

119.37.0.en: (And I will walk at liberty: for I seek thy precepts.

119.37.1.en: 1- David wishes to receive the enlarged heart; because he seeks God's commandments in order to live by them, his heart is enlarged with love for everyone, even for his enemies, as he did with Saul and Absalom, who tried to kill him.

119.37.2.en: 2- The enlarged heart gives its owner rest, joy and thanksgiving, whatever problems or afflictions he meets, as happened with Paul in the city of Corinth (2 Cor 6:11-13).

119.38.0.en: (I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed.

119.38.1.en: 1- Since David's heart was filled with faith and the love of God, he dared and bore witness to God before kings, such as Saul and the kings of the Philistines, and did not fear their vengeance. The Three Youths and Daniel did likewise, and in the New Testament Paul before the kings who tried him, and he did not fear or feel ashamed before them.

119.39.0.en: (And I will delight myself in thy commandments, which I have loved. My hands also will I lift up unto thy commandments, which I have loved; and I will meditate in thy statutes.

119.39.1.en: 1- David loved God's commandments, so that he delighted in reading them, meditating on them and repeating them; that is, his heart and mouth moved together with his mind in enjoying the word of God. Then he lifted his hands to God's commandments, declaring his holding fast to them and his readiness to act on them, so his prayer, in which he lifts his hands, is nourished and turns into good works that his hands do; so that in the end he communes with God, singing of His statutes and worship, that is, he praises God always.

119.39.2.en: Take care to bear witness to the word of God, not only in your life in which the commandment speaks, but also in the words of love that come from your mouth to everyone, together with praise and thanksgiving to God with all your energy.

119.39.3.en: The seventh section (Zayin): Comfort in affliction (vv. 49-56). The aim:

119.39.4.en: After bearing witness to the word of God, he needed always to remember His word, to keep it in his ways, especially in afflictions, when the proud gather around him. So he needed to sing to God and hold fast to His worship, and even remember Him in the night and meditate on His word.

119.40.0.en: (Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope. This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.

119.40.1.en: 1- When David entered affliction he had nothing before him but to take refuge in God, and he reminded Him of His promises to him, that He might save him from his sufferings; not because God had forgotten, but so that David might declare his faith and his need of God. And because of this humility and longing for the word of God, He must rescue him from his humiliation.

119.40.2.en: 2- God's word supports the person in affliction, and even gives him life, grants him peace, and then brings him out of his distress.

119.41.0.en: (The proud have had me greatly in derision: yet have I not declined from thy law. I remembered thy judgments of old, O LORD; and have comforted myself.

119.41.1.en: 1- David faced mockery and doubts from the wicked proud, not only against himself but against his God and His commandments, but he remained holding fast to God's commandments, and even began to remind himself of God's judgments in preserving His children from of old. His heart was comforted as he remembered how God preserved righteous Noah during the Flood, and Abram and Lot at the war with Chedorlaomer, and preserved Abram and Isaac in Egypt and in Gerar, and preserved Jacob from the evil of his uncle Laban... Thus David did not resist the wicked proud, but directed his heart to the positive work, which is remembering God's judgments and holding fast to His commandments.

119.42.0.en: (Horror hath taken hold upon me because of the wicked that forsake thy law.

119.42.1.en: Horror: the heart burning with grief.

119.42.2.en: 1- David's heart was touched and grieved over the sinners who forsook the law of God, because they of course have no peace in their hearts, and eternal torment awaits them, since they forsook God's law deliberately and not out of ignorance, as Paul grieved over Demas (2 Tim 4:10) and as Samuel and Elijah grieved over the people of God (1 Sam 7:3-5; 1 Kgs 18:40). May we grieve and pray for everyone around us who departs from the way of God.

119.43.0.en: (Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage.

119.43.1.en: 1- Here David turned positively to God, and did not surrender to his grief over the wicked, but took care to perform God's statutes, that is, the rites of worship, which expressed the rejoicing of his heart and his praise of God in the midst of the exile of the world, as he felt the many around him who were departing from God, but his comfort was his sense of God who is with him. Thus David rejoices and the heart of God rejoices in this praise and this worship that the wicked have abandoned, so David became like a candle in the midst of darkness, giving hope to the righteous, and perhaps the wicked will return to God and repent.

119.44.0.en: (I have remembered thy name, O LORD, in the night, and have kept thy law. This I had, because I kept thy precepts.

119.44.1.en: 1- The prophet David was accustomed to pray throughout the day, before he began his work, and during the work, and when he went in to sleep on his bed, and also in the night he remembered God's name and His commandments and meditated on them. The quiet of the night helps him to meditate. On the other hand, the night signifies afflictions and the darkness of sin, so when he remembers the word of God he relies on it and keeps away from every evil.

119.44.2.en: 2- Because of David's occupation with God's law and commandments he delighted in them, experienced God's power in his life, and enjoyed inner peace. He obtained all these blessings because of his keeping God's commandments, repeating them and meditating on them.

119.44.3.en: Do not forget to pray at night before you sleep, and God will give you quiet sleep; and if you wish, you can seek God if you wake in the night, even for a few minutes, and so receive more abundant blessings.

119.44.4.en: The eighth section (Heth): Pleasing God, my portion (vv. 57-64). The aim:

119.44.5.en: After David was comforted in his affliction he felt that the Lord is his portion, and tried to please Him by walking in His commandments, thanking Him and learning His worship.

119.45.0.en: (Thou art my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.

119.45.1.en: 1- David felt that his portion is the Lord, and not the possessions of the world or its lusts, and he devoted himself to keeping God's commandments and applying them in his life. Although he lives in the world and does many works, his one goal is clear before him, to live by the word of God.

119.45.2.en: 2- The tribe of Levi had the Lord as its portion, so it did not possess land in Canaan (Deut 18:1), and likewise the consecrated in the New Testament, the priests, monks and servants; all of these God satisfies with His love, and they do not need material things, since they made their goal keeping the word of God for their lives, and conveying it to others.

119.46.0.en: (I intreated thy favour with my whole heart: be merciful unto me according to thy word.

119.46.1.en: 1- David feels that he is a sinner, and wants to please God, and his love for God appears in his striving with all his heart, not only his striving with bodily works but accompanied by feelings and thought, to declare truly his need of God, so God intervenes with His mercies according to His promise to accept His children who are disciplined.

119.46.2.en: 2- Here the integration of the work of striving with grace appears, and also reliance on God in asking for His mercy, not in a particular form, but according to the word of God, that is, what God sees fit for him He gives him.

119.46.3.en: 3- The face of God refers to the incarnate Christ, for no one has seen God, but the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He hath declared Him. So David in the spirit of prophecy saw Christ, and tries to please Him by repentance and prayer.

119.47.0.en: (I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies. I made haste, and delayed not to keep thy commandments.

119.47.1.en: 1- One of David's virtues is that he always reviews himself, so he thinks about the ways he walks, that is, his life and all his occupations, and if he finds that any of them has taken him away from God, he returns quickly to God's commandments and testimonies, for he cannot bear to be far from God. This shows:

119.47.2.en: 1- David's care for the word of God, for it is the foundation of his life.

119.47.3.en: 2- David's courage in changing his works and directions if they deviate from God.

119.47.4.en: 3- His concern to hasten to correct his course; because if he delays he may not be able to return to God, and may forget what he was convinced of and be swept along with the current and the occupations of the world.

119.48.0.en: (The bands of the wicked have robbed me: but I have not forgotten thy law.

119.48.1.en: 1- The bands of the wicked are their opposition to David, the devices of the devil, and all the threats of harming him. These bands can hinder any person from his spiritual striving. But David's strength was gained from his holding fast to God's law, which is stronger than all the bands of the wicked, indeed they are nothing before the power of the word of God, on which David relied, and which he repeated and meditated on every day, so it did not leave his mind, but was in his heart.

119.49.0.en: (At midnight I will rise to give thanks unto thee because of thy righteous judgments.

119.49.1.en: 1- David's heart was occupied with prayer throughout the day, and when he slept at night he could not leave prayer, so he rose to praise God and thank Him for His care of him; perhaps he did not go quickly to his bed, but continued for a time praying even while on his bed, for prayer had drawn his heart by day and by night, and praise and glorification had become his delight.

119.49.2.en: 2- If the night signifies afflictions, David also rises from them to thank God who keeps him during the affliction. And if the night signifies falling into sin, David repents of it, then thanks God who lifted him from sin to repentance.

119.50.0.en: (I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy precepts.

119.50.1.en: 1- David loved the Lord and lived in His fear, so that he loved all who fear Him, and was joined to them and accompanied them to be encouraged by them and to encourage them. And these who fear God, it is God who established them in His fear, He kept them in His commandments.

119.50.2.en: 2- The One who can accompany all who fear the Lord is Christ, who is the head of the body, and all who fear God are members of His body. So this verse is a prophecy about Christ, which David speaks in the voice of Christ.

119.51.0.en: (The earth, O LORD, is full of thy mercy: teach me thy statutes.

119.51.1.en: 1- David realized that God's mercy has filled the whole earth, that is, covered all people. For God's kindnesses to all people are in the sun that shines, the air they breathe, the earth He established for them... and therefore, in response to God's mercy, he asks God to teach him His worship so that he may reach Him and thank Him with all his heart.

119.51.2.en: 2- God's mercy filled the whole earth through the Cross, which offered redemption for all mankind, for everyone who believes in Him, so that it may come out of its evils and live for Him in holy worship in His Church.

119.51.3.en: 3- When a person learns the statutes of his God he becomes, like God, merciful to all around him, and not only the righteous, so he is a light to the world, and they see in him the light of Christ.
